mike: Quick share — I ran the canary perf run for the new P95 SLO-driven token-budgeting by route/tier. Putting notes + raw snippets here for visibility.

mike: Experiment setup: dynamic_token_budget = base_budget * (1 + tier_scale). Canary deployed to us-west-2 (4x A100), model=redwood-v2-slim-8b-quant, KV cache warmup ~75% hit. Queue policy: default-joiner, batch_window_ms=8.

mike: Summary numbers (baseline vs canary): p50 28ms -> 27ms, p95 310ms -> 245ms, p99 520ms -> 490ms. Throughput +6% nominal. Notable: p95 improvement but we saw a new tail source for short (<50 token) requests being delayed/joined with long streams.

sasha: Can you paste the profiler traces / kernel decisions? Any kernel-selection churn during those tails?

mike: Paste of relevant excerpt from the profiler (trimmed):
```
kernel_selector: seq_len_thresholds: { fp16_threshold: 256, int8_threshold: 1024 }
batch_summary: microbatch_sizes: [1,1,2,8,12,1,1]
kernel_switch_events: [t=0.12s -> fp16, t=0.32s -> int8 on large microbatch]
latency_breakdown: kv_lookup_ms: [p50=1.2, p95=12.1, p99=18.4]
```

mike: Observations: the selector is flipping to int8 kernels when a large request joins a microbatch, which increases per-token overhead for the shorter concurrent requests. Also KV lookup p95 jumped to ~12ms (baseline ~4ms) — looks like contention during batch formation.

anya: That KV lookup bump looks familiar — PR #3124 that unified queue locks caused a hot path in cache access under high join rates. Might be the regression.

sasha: Agreed. Two quick proposals: 1) prefer fp16 for seq < 256 OR when microbatch_size < 8 to avoid excessive kernel switching for short requests; 2) revert/unwind the lock path from #3124 in the canary or add optimistic reads for the KV cache.

mike: Tried an immediate canary tweak: set kernel preference override and queue_policy=prefer-first (avoid aggressive joining). Ran a short 1-hour canary. Results: p95 -> 245ms, p99 -> 490ms, throughput +4%. But I noticed increased early_cutoff on free-tier routes (we clipped some low-budget requests).

ying: For tiering, we should enforce a per-tier floor on token_budget (e.g., floor=8 tokens for free tier) so we don't early-cut short requests. The scaling should be additive: budget = max(floor, base * scale).

mike: I also instrumented queue traces. Example:
```
queue_event: { req_id: abc, tier: free, enqueue_t=0.003, joined_with: [long-req-xyz], wait_ms: 9.4 }
cache_lock_wait_ms: 95th=10.9
```
This shows short free-tier reqs waiting almost the full batch window because they attempt to join long-running streams.

anya: Sounds like we need route-aware batch windows. Suggest config: low-tier max_wait_ms=5, default=8, high-tier=12. Keeps short requests from accumulating with long ones.

sasha: Also add a kernel selection guard: if any microbatch contains >50% requests with seq < 128, avoid switching to int8 even if average seq crosses threshold. That reduces churn.

mike: Action plan I'm going to run:
- Open perf ticket referencing PR #3124 and attach traces.
- Revert/unwind lock change for canary (quick revert) and run 24h.
- Expose kernel thresholds as runtime tunables (fp16_threshold, int8_threshold, microbatch_switch_guard).
- Patch token_budget algo to use floor + scale_by_tier and set low-tier floor=8.
- AB test route-aware batch windows: {low:5, default:8, high:12}.

perf-bot: Perf run summary (run-id: 2026-02-11-1765): metrics: p95_before=310ms p95_after=245ms delta=-65ms. p50 stable. CI perf alerts: 0.

oncall-sre: I'll watch the canary dashboards and add an alert for KV lookup p95>8ms and p95 latency regressions >10% for any route. Tagging SRE oncall. @sre-team :eyes:

mike: Thanks — will post the PRs and the AB split config in a follow-up. For visibility, PRs to look at: runtime#4218 (kernel tunables), runtime#4219 (queue_policy revert), routing#2043 (tiered token floors).

anya: Great. If the canary holds, plan a staged rollout: 10% routes -> 30% -> 100% over 48h, with automatic rollback if p95 degrades by 5% relative to canary baseline.

sasha: One more ask: add a microprofiler tag when kernel switches happen so we can correlate exact request IDs to kernel changes in future runs. Quick code snippet suggestion: `Tracer.annotate(req_id, "kernel_switch", {from: fp16, to: int8, at_ms: 320})`.

mike: Will add that to runtime#4218. Thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: Follow-up will include full AB metrics after 24h and a condensed table of per-route p95 changes.
